references.text: The Sabbath commandment in the Ten Commandments. The women 'kept themselves according to the command' (κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν), referring back to God's instruction to keep the Sabbath holy ([ref:2 Mos 20:8-11|Exodus 20:8-11]).
An early example of Sabbath rest as a command from the Lord. The people were to remain at rest on the seventh day, just as the women observed Sabbath rest ([ref:2 Mos 16:23-30|Exodus 16:23-30]).
The Sabbath commandment repeated in Deuteronomy. The women followed 'the command' (ἐντολήν), which includes this formulation of the Sabbath instruction ([ref:5 Mos 5:12-15|Deuteronomy 5:12-15]).
The immediate context: The Sabbath was about to begin, and the women who had come from Galilee saw the tomb and how Jesus' body was laid there ([ref:Luk 23:54-55|Luke 23:54-55]).
After the Sabbath, on the first day of the week, the women came to the tomb with the fragrant spices (ἀρώματα) they had prepared, but found the tomb empty ([ref:Luk 24:1-3|Luke 24:1-3]).
Mark's parallel account: After the Sabbath was over, the women bought fragrant spices to anoint Jesus and came early on the first day of the week to the tomb ([ref:Mark 16:1-2|Mark 16:1-2]).
Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where Jesus was laid. They took note of the place so they could return after the Sabbath ([ref:Mark 15:47|Mark 15:47]).

John reports that Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes to anoint Jesus' body according to Jewish burial custom, paralleling the women's preparation of spices and ointments ([ref:Joh 19:39-40|John 19:39-40]).
The women who followed Jesus from Galilee and served him, including Mary Magdalene, are the same ones now preparing fragrant spices and ointments for his burial ([ref:Luk 8:2-3|Luke 8:2-3]).
The Sabbath commandment with a prohibition against working on the Sabbath day. The women's rest 'according to the command' reflects this prohibition against work ([ref:2 Mos 35:2-3|Exodus 35:2-3]).
